question: For the patient who has the highest Ig A within the normal range, what is his or her diagnosis?
evidence: highest Ig A within the normal range refers to MAX(IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500);
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0 FROM (SELECT patientData.Diagnosis AS c0, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY labData.IGA DESC) AS __r FROM Patient AS patientData INNER JOIN Laboratory AS labData ON patientData.ID = labData.ID WHERE labData.IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT patientData.Diagnosis FROM Patient AS patientData INNER JOIN Laboratory AS labData ON patientData.ID = labData.ID WHERE labData.IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500 ORDER BY labData.IGA DESC LIMIT 1

c.sql: SELECT p.Diagnosis FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.IGA = (SELECT MAX(IGA) FROM Laboratory WHERE IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500)

d.request: What are the diagnoses of all patients tied for the highest Ig A level within the normal range of 80–500?
d.sql: SELECT p.Diagnosis FROM Patient AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.IGA = (SELECT MAX(IGA) FROM Laboratory WHERE IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500))

b.request: Return the patient diagnosis for every Laboratory row whose IGA is the highest value from 80 to 500 inclusive, including all rows tied at that value
b.sql: SELECT p.Diagnosis FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.IGA = (SELECT MAX(IGA) FROM Laboratory WHERE IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500)
